#                         Fixed by the IP tables paste.
#  2. mgmt-acl ACCESS     extra: entries of the unit's list that are not in the standard's (the paste
#                         replaces the list: they are gone afterwards) (e.g. iptables -A INPUT -s
#                         10.0.31.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT). Fixed by the IP tables paste (it
#                         replaces every entry: this one is gone afterwards).
# Consistent: snmp, aaa. Not planned: breakglass (walkthrough Step 10).
# Secrets: 2 present on the device, not changed (--secrets pushes them).

# Note: aaa: 13 statements of the device's own, kept on purpose.
# Note: snmp: 4 statements of the device's own, kept on purpose.
# WARNING: the IP tables list has no final DROP and no INPUT policy DROP: it restricts nothing until
# the last step of the walkthrough is applied.
# WARNING: the pull saw 1 other session on the unit: the paste is live for them too; type /SN before
# you paste and make sure no other administrator is working on it.
# The unit has no commit-confirm and no rollback: every value is live as soon as its Enter is
# accepted, and the configuration is written to flash when a top-level menu is left with ESC (any
# session that leaves one saves everything). tacctl types nothing: you do each step yourself.
# Before you start: keep the serial console, or a second session logged in as an Administrator, open
# until the check at the end passes; type /SN and make sure no other administrator is on the unit (the
# pull saw 1 other session).
# The way back is tacctl device config plan lab-unit --backout: the old values and the old IP tables
# list as a block (or the slots to clear).

# Type this first, on lab-unit, and check the version:   /H
# The title must read "COMMAND MENU: Version 8.10": tacctl's tables are those of that command menu,
# and another version may number its pages differently: stop. /J shows the unit's Site ID: the pull
# read wti.site.example.net; another one means this is not the unit.

##### IP TABLES (replaces every entry; see the notes): lab-unit #####
# Do this from the serial session or one you can afford to lose: the list is the unit's firewall,
# and a wrong one cuts off every way in.
# At the /N menu type 5 and Enter, then paste the block below as it stands (<iptables> to
# </iptables>, at the left margin) at the page's prompt. The unit answers "Configuring iptables -
# Please wait...".
# The paste REPLACES every entry the unit holds (20 entries now) with 20 entries, all rendered by
# tacctl. The unit's list has no tail (no final DROP, no INPUT policy), so this list restricts
# nothing until the walkthrough's last step is pasted by you (Step 11: tacctl device config show
# lab-unit).
# It is live when the unit takes it; there is no commit-confirm. Leaving /N with ESC (any session
# that does) writes it to flash: wait for "Saving configuration to flash". Check at once from a
# second session, and from an address outside the list: it must be refused.
# The way back is: tacctl device config plan lab-unit --backout (the old list as a block, or the
# slots to clear).
<iptables>
iptables -A INPUT -i lo -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -m conntrack --ctstate ESTABLISHED,RELATED -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.100.0/23 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.20.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.34 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.34 -p udp --dport 161:162 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.36 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.28.36 -p udp --dport 161:162 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.30.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.40.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.50.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.60.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.70.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.90.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.0.120.0/24 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 192.0.2.14 -p udp --dport 161:162 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -s 10.1.101.0/24 -p udp --dport 161 -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.1.100.0/23 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 10.0.0.0/16 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
iptables -A INPUT -i eth0 -s 192.0.2.14 -p icmp -j ACCEPT
</iptables>
##### END OF IP TABLES: lab-unit #####
